as_told.title: Luis Alvarez's asteroid impact theory of the dinosaur extinction

plain: The dinosaurs died out 66 million years ago when a comet or asteroid struck the Earth, a theory put forward by Luis and Walter Alvarez in the 1980s and, as this story tells it, ridiculed at first. The journalist Graham Hancock tells Michels that "nobody disputes now" the impact, and that the Chicxulub crater, deeply buried beneath the land and sea of the Yucatan, is the evidence. In another conversation Hancock stresses that the idea "still wasn't accepted until they found the crater", which he places in the Gulf of Mexico. Michels tells it himself as Luis Alvarez's theory alone, without the crater or the mockery. The tellers bring it up as an example of a scorned idea that turned out to be accepted once the evidence was found.
